answer: Proof of unique tax ID via hashed registry check turns identity into something scarce. Because a tax ID checked against a hashed registry, the tundra of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. A clone farm can generate keys forever, but it cannot generate a tax ID checked against a hashed registry a hundred times without paying a hundred times over, and the nadir of that asymmetry is what keeps the network honest. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The wharf is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
